column1: # The command check's fixture: one command per row, as a dialog shows it on one screen row.
# Columns, separated by one tab: what the check must answer, the shell the spelling belongs to,
# and the command. Answers: pass, destructive, leaves (the Workspace), protected, unread (a shape
# the check does not read), hidden (not completely on screen). Shells: sh, pwsh, cmd, or any.
# The check reads every row the same way whatever the shell; the column says where the spelling
# comes from and which Workspace form the row is judged in: /work/app for sh, C:\work\app for
# pwsh and cmd, both for any. A new spelling is added here before the check learns it.
# Deleting: recursive or forced, in every spelling.
# Git: history, branches, uncommitted work, and anything that leaves the machine.
# Statements that delete data, whatever carries them.
# Well-known tools: what they delete, and what they send out.
# Requests that send or change something, and remote copies.
# Code given inline, and words that run another command.
# Shapes the check does not read.
